question: Which phonemes of the Mālinī are placed on the head, eyes, nose, seals, and ears?
premises: The letters na, ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, and ḹ are assigned to the crest and the head-garland.
The letter tha is assigned to the top of the head.
The eyes above and below receive other placements, ī is placed on the nose, ṇu and ṇū on the two seals, and the two ears receive their letters.
inference: Verse 121 continues the Mālinī nyāsa by mapping specific phonemes onto upper head, eye, nasal, seal, and ear locations.
uncertainties: The exact parsing of 'cordhve dho@nye' as applied to the eyes is compressed and may imply paired upper and lower eye placements.
The term 'mudre' may refer to specific ritual hand-seals or to bodily apertures; the nyāsa context suggests paired locations.
plain_english: Place na, ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, and ḹ on the crest and the garland of the head, and tha on the crown. Assign the eyes above and below, place ī on the nose, ṇu and ṇū on the two seals, and place the corresponding letters on the two ears.
